en.title: Numbers with Exactly Three Positive Divisors
en.description:
If a positive integer has exactly 3 positive divisors, it must be the square of a prime. For each given upper bound x, output how many such numbers do not exceed x.



This site adds a standard input/output protocol; this does not mean the original function-style problem had this protocol.
en.input: The first line contains q (1 ≤ q ≤ 100000), followed by q lines with one integer x each (1 ≤ x ≤ 25000000000000).
en.output: For each query, output on its own line the number of positive integers from 1 to x (inclusive) that have exactly 3 positive divisors.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the problem rules, approach, and proof.
hints: A number with exactly 3 divisors is exactly the square of a prime. Sieve the primes up to the largest square root; for each query, count primes using the integer square root and binary search.
